This file is the owner-decision side of the invariant; scripts/run_book_supervisor.ps1 is the mechanism side. src/safety/armed_set.py reconciles the two and tests/safety/test_armed_set_single_source.py enforces that they agree. authority.mechanism: scripts/run_book_supervisor.ps1 supplies run_book.py --tags / --frontier-exits / --spread-geometry-floor. There is no confidence floor that can express the armed set (CLAUDE.md section 4; admission.py:218-219), so --tags IS the arming mechanism.
authority.rule: an owner arming decision changes THIS FILE and the launcher in the same commit; a launcher edit with no matching declaration fails the test, and a declaration the launcher does not implement fails the same test.

safety_notes.empty_tags_is_fail_open: run_book.py:383 -- `args.tags.split(...) if args.tags else None` -- so tags="" is falsy and the book runs ALL BUILT sleeves. An empty tag list is therefore UNBOUNDED, never empty. armed_set.py models this as tags=None and the reconciler reports it as a fail-open, not as a four-sleeve match.
safety_notes.all_typo_tags_is_fail_closed_but_mute: registry.py:144 drops unknown tags with no fallback and no error, so an all-typo --tags stands the book down silently every tick.
safety_notes.tags_can_only_subset: book_engine.py:452-453 intersects --tags with the include-flag registry, so --tags can never add back a sleeve the config removed.
safety_notes.this_file_does_not_enter_the_activation_: activation_token.config_digest_for (activation_token.py:1089-1116) hashes config/agent_config.yaml plus the active profile file BYTES only. Adding or editing this file does NOT invalidate either account's token and does NOT require a re-mint.
safety_notes.this_file_does_not_enter_the_r2_executio: replay_acceleration_attempt5_typed_sparse_runner.py:1502-1511 declares config_file_hashes as an explicit two-entry dict (config/agent_config.yaml, config/profiles/operator_profile.yaml). It does not glob config/, so this file is outside the seal.
safety_notes.surface_production_vs_experiment: An account row carries `surface`: `production` is the armed book at the production risk dial under broker identity magic 20260401; `experiment` is a minimal-size surface (run_book.py --f5-minimal-size-usd) that places a fixed few dollars per trade under its own broker identity (magic 0, comment prefix 'F5:') in its own namespace. armed_set.armed_sleeves() unions PRODUCTION rows only, because that is what every caller has ever meant by 'armed'. The launcher side derives the surface from whether the row passes --f5-minimal-size-usd, so a production row that quietly gained that flag is a reconcile() surface_mismatch and a build failure -- it would otherwise place 1/200th lots while every published figure still priced it at the dial.
